chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from one of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The people of kindness in the world are the people of kindness in the Hereafter. It will be said to them: 'Indeed, your sins have been forgiven for you, so gift your good deeds to whomever you wish.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the good deeds of those who perform acts of kindness in the world?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the transformative power of consistent righteous conduct (ma'ruf), linking worldly benevolence directly to divine recognition in the Hereafter. It describes a unique eschatological state where sins are forgiven, granting the believer the spiritual authority to gift their accumulated good deeds to whomever they wish, reflecting the concept of 'Hibb al-Hasanat'. This highlights the interplay between individual merit and the social utility of good deeds in Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, from one of our companions, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The people (performers) of the acts of kindness, they are the people of the acts of kindness in the Hereafter. It would be said to them: ‘Your sins have been Forgiven for you, so you can gift your good deeds to whomsoever you so desire to’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu ‘Abd Allah al-Barqiy from certain individuals of our people in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

providers of Benevolent Assistance will be as such on the Day of Judgment also. They will receive the news, ‘Your sins are all forgiven. You may give away your good deeds as gifts to whomever you like.”’
